resources.memory_binding: Unchanged: no explicit membind; taskset CPU0-7 plus external NUMA page observation

config.runtime: vLLM0.11.2 fixed WiSP cap16 BF16 with common batched map; prefetch/dynamic off; one next prefill chunk action
config.holdout_scope: Next two source entries [10,11] after previously observed 0..9 in this paging chain; old pair [4,5] retained. Prepared project articles, not a globally untouched dataset. No holdout outcome inspected before freezing.

first_action_payload.boundary: Host counter deltas for first mixed and next branch call times fixed per-expert tensor bytes; read tax separate; no pure memcpy or wire claim

config.total_payload: Sum final_worker pager_layers weight_copy_payload_bytes after measurement counter reset; complete episode includes preaction prefix; bytes are copied tensor bytes, not PCIe wire bytes
config.question: On two preselected unseen incoming documents, does fixed first16-next8-then16 offer a repeatable full-request tradeoff beyond static8/16/32 and phase8?
config.reference_rule: Common pre-injection incumbent state across all cells; one8 only: common after-first16 logical state within each document. Different baseline shapes independently regenerate subsequent states.
config.retention: Keep every episode including first; stop on first failure; all raw remote; safe numeric/hash export only
config.measurement_control: Same LLM/CUDA context/pinned-master/scratch/map/KV allocations, native schedule restored, drained KV queue sorted and pager state emptied before identical warmup; all control costs retained separately and excluded from episode by original measurement boundary; same tiny pinned map buffers/events in both arms; no profiler; map stats reset before measurement and final GPU map validation after wall receipt; actual expert bytes/LRU/output hashes compared; new single prebranch snapshot in every arm remains in episode wall; only selected next prefill chunk differs, later state regenerated
config.interpretation: Fixed one8 rule selected before holdout; no feedback selector or future counter use. Compare full wall, old maxITL and incoming TTFT; one8 pays its extra snapshot/observation costs.
config.correction: ensure_calls counts expert subgroups; verify 16 layer entries, positive subgroup calls and nonnegative deltas, not subgroup count==16
config.workload_reconstruction: Construct exactly three rows from the hash-verified existing remote source; per-group source_indices specify old/old/incoming; only code/config and hashes uploaded.

design.primary: Full episode wall vs incumbent max-ITL vs incoming TTFT, comparing fixed one8 with every strongest declared simple arm in each document/block.
design.negative_control: Static16 and other unchanged arm repeats report temporal drift; no sample maximum is a population noise bound.
design.replication_boundary: Two documents by five strategies by two randomized blocks, n=2 per document/strategy; tiny exploratory holdout, no production tail estimate or noninferiority.
design.decision: If fixed one8 has reproducible residual beyond this finite simple comparison set, next step is continuous arrivals with overhead counted, no further tiny threshold scan. If dominated/no stable residual, stop this fixed-position rule, keep problem open; ambiguous drift remains inconclusive.
design.prebranch_capture: Only one8 needs the extra after-first16 snapshot; its cost remains in wall/gaps. Baselines use their original observation level, never subtract overhead.

frozen_prediction.recent_mixed: Predicted branch duration = first completed mixed duration * curve_s[next_chunk] / curve_s[16].
frozen_prediction.online_visibility: Predictions saved before next action; first mixed counter/duration only. No later calls or outcomes.
frozen_prediction.prediction_use: Diagnostic of action costs, not post-hoc selection of best arm; no expert predictor added.
